{"id":"JMAP-cayv.13","title":"RFC 9457 problem details: cite 9457, title/instance/Content-Language, helpers for every HTTP resource, client parsing, testjig","description":"RFC 9457 problem details everywhere:
- Code: cite RFC 9457 instead of 7807 in jmap-types/src/error.rs (lines 10, 129, 387, 401), jmap-server/src/response.rs, testjig http.rs and ws.rs. A grep for 'RFC ?7807' finds them all.
- jmap-server response.rs ProblemDetails gains optional `title` and `instance`, Content-Type application/problem+json, and optional Content-Language when title/detail are localized (from CallerCtx Accept-Language, decision .1(h)).
- Add public helpers so consumers can produce problem details for non-API resources: Session, upload, download, event source, WS handshake failure, extension endpoints. The draft says every JMAP HTTP resource SHOULD.
- jmap-base-client: parse a problem details body from ANY of those responses into a typed error. Today it may parse only API request errors; check. Clients act on `type` and the HTTP status code, never on title/detail.
- testjig: return problem details on every 4xx/5xx, including Session, eventsource, WS handshake, upload and download, and test each.
- New type URIs that extensions define go in the JMAP Error Codes registry, prefixed urn:ietf:params:jmap:error: (RFC 8620 9.5). Audit existing extension error codes for the prefix in problem details.

Audit: every request-level JMAP error goes through ProblemDetails::for_jmap_error, which always prefixes urn:ietf:params:jmap:error:; no extension crate emits its own problem bodies. 401/403 keep ClientError::AuthFailed and 429 RateLimited (unchanged), so Problem covers the other 4xx/5xx. testjig has no upload/download resources, so none to cover there.
